subject: physics
title: Units, prefixes and standard form
key_idea: Every physical quantity has an **SI unit**. Prefixes such as kilo and milli scale a unit up or down by a power of ten. To convert units, multiply or divide by the right factor. Very large and very small numbers are written in **standard form**.

blocks.text: Physics calculations only work when every quantity is in the right unit. This section covers the SI units and the prefixes that scale them.

items.meaning: The standard unit for a quantity, such as the metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s) and newton (N).
A letter placed before a unit that multiplies it by a power of ten.
A larger unit, such as the kilometre (km).
A smaller unit, such as the millimetre (mm).

items: Use the SI unit in a calculation unless the question tells you otherwise.
A prefix is a power of ten: kilo is 1000, milli is one thousandth.
Know giga, mega, kilo, centi, milli, micro and nano.

blocks.text: Convert a quantity into the unit an equation needs. Change one unit at a time and check that the answer makes sense.

items.text: For example 1 km = 1000 m, 1 min = 60 s, or 1 h = 60 × 60 s = 3600 s.
To change km to m, multiply by 1000. To change m to km, divide by 1000.
To change hours to seconds, multiply by 3600. To change seconds to hours, divide by 3600.
A smaller unit gives a bigger number. A larger unit gives a smaller number.

items: km/h to m/s: multiply by 1000, then divide by 3600. This is the same as dividing by 3.6.
m/s to km/h: multiply by 3600, then divide by 1000. This is the same as multiplying by 3.6.

diagram.alt: Convert a speed from kilometres per hour to metres per second.
diagram.question: A car travels at {v} km/h. Calculate its speed in m/s.

items: Write down the unit link first, such as 1 km = 1000 m.
To convert hours to seconds, multiply by 60 × 60 = 3600.
Converting km/h to m/s means dividing by 3.6.

blocks.text: Calculators give long answers. Round them sensibly and write very large or very small numbers in standard form.

items: The first significant figure is the first digit that is not zero.
Count along from there. 0.00540 has three significant figures.
To round, look at the next digit. If it is 5 or more, round up.
Give an answer to the same number of significant figures as the data, or one more.

blocks.text: For example, 5.555 m/s is 5.6 m/s to 2 significant figures.

blocks.label: Standard form
where: A is a number from 1 up to (but not including) 10.
n is a whole number. It is negative for numbers smaller than 1.

items: 150 000 000 km = 1.5 × 10⁸ km. Move the decimal point 8 places left.
0.000 009 s = 9 × 10⁻⁶ s. Move the decimal point 6 places right.
2.45 × 10⁹ Hz = 2 450 000 000 Hz. A positive power makes the number bigger.
Count significant figures from the first non-zero digit.
In standard form, A is between 1 and 10.
A negative power of ten means the number is smaller than 1.

checks.q: Convert 2 kW into watts and 1.5 mW into watts.
A car travels at 72 km/h. Calculate its speed in m/s.
Write 0.000 009 s in standard form and 5.555 m/s to 2 significant figures.

worked_example.question:
Microwaves from a mobile phone take 0.000 009 s to reach a mobile phone mast.
speed of microwaves = 300 000 000 m/s

Calculate the distance between the mobile phone and the mobile phone mast.
Use the equation: distance = speed × time
worked_example.tip: One mark for the correct substitution and one mark for the answer, 2700 m.

worked_example.question:
A speed limit sign from a European motorway shows speeds in km/h (kilometres per hour).
The sign shows a speed of 130 km/h.

Show that a speed of 31 m/s is less than a speed of 130 km/h.
answer_points: Convert either the distance or the time: 31 m = 31/1000 km = 0.031 km, or 1 s = 1/3600 h
Evaluate: 31 m/s = 110 km/h, or 130 km/h = 36(.1) m/s
Compare in one unit: 110 km/h is less than 130 km/h
worked_example.tip: One mark for converting a unit and one mark for the evaluation. A correct answer without working still scores full marks.

worked_example.question:
A student records the current through a lamp.
State the unit for current.
worked_example.tip: The symbol I is the quantity, not the unit, so it does not score.

blocks.text: Learn the unit and symbol for each quantity below. They are used across the whole course.

items: Time can also be given in minutes (min) and hours (h). Convert to seconds before using an equation: 1 min = 60 s and 1 h = 3600 s.
Length can be given in centimetres (cm). Divide by 100 to change cm to m.
